turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so you have twenty minutes. Owen found out about that zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first.
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.

"The end of it." A machine's guess, and the company that sells it says in writing not to use it as the sole basis for punishing a student. Your own procedure 4.3 says the same thing, so withdraw the zero or I'm going upstairs.
I don't need more proof than that.
"You don't need more proof." I'm writing that down. Then we're done here and I'm going straight to the principal, unless you have something you can actually put in front of me.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
"Unlike some people." My child never lies, Hale. Are you calling him a liar, or me?

Then the principal hears today that you entered a zero without calling home, against procedure 4.2, on nothing but a software score. If that doesn't satisfy me, it goes to the board under section 42. Last chance to show me a document, Hale.
